phrases.text: November, 2025.
Cyclone Ditwah tears across Sri Lanka.
Now look north. Off the Jaffna coast, four islands keep their own lights on.
Delft.
Nainativu.
Analaitivu.
Eluvaitivu.
No cable to the mainland.
Every drop of fuel arrives by boat.
Around 9,000 people live here. A hospital. A water plant.
Last year, these grids burned 975,000 litres of diesel,
for nearly three gigawatt-hours
at up to 118 rupees a unit.
Now imagine the storm hits. The operators are evacuated.
The data goes dark.
And the grid has to decide on its own.
Hand that call to an ordinary AI, and it answers with total confidence. Even when it's wrong. One bad call, and the whole island goes black.
So we asked a different question. What if the AI knew when it didn't know?
This is MetaCore.
It reads the grid as a living graph of weather, load and generation.
It measures its own doubt.
When the answer is clear, it acts fast.
When it isn't, it slows down, and thinks.
And here's the part we're proudest of. Before any action touches the grid, a deterministic physics firewall replays it on a digital twin.
Voltage.
Line loading.
Generation.
Convergence.
Every action gets a verdict.
Approve.
Reject.
Or unverified, with its risk attached.
Nothing executes without approval, and every rejection teaches the agent why.
Same storm. Same proposal.
This time, the doubt is caught.
The unsafe action is blocked.
And the lights stay on.
We built this for the Ceylon Electricity Board.
For the families on these islands.
And for every remote, coastal grid that simply cannot afford a guess.
MetaCore.
It knows when it doesn't know.
And it verifies, before it acts.
